releases.title: Beta release candidate: RAM card, a calm loopback cable, Feedback and any USB stick
features: When the music USB goes out, a deck playing its whole track from RAM shows a card in place of its waveform: WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE, and how to get the waveform back. Title, time, BPM, tempo, key, lamps and hot cues stay on screen. This works on every deck, in MODERN and CLASSIC.
The loopback cable's E-8307 hub warning is gone. XZ Mods never shows it as an error, and in CLASSIC the player's window becomes a calm LOOPBACK CABLE CONNECTED card.

Feedback has its own place at the foot of the app rail on every page. Report a problem, request a feature or ask a question there, and follow everything you sent in My reports. A count shows reports waiting from your XZ.
The app is laid out as a tool: a compact header, Tools grouped into Your USB, Your XZ and This app, and the version at the foot of the rail.

The window opens at a size that fits your screen and can shrink to 760 x 520. Every step of the USB guide has a Back button, and Cancel or Back from the first step opens a list of the USB sticks plugged in, with Write to a folder instead at the end.
The loader can go on any writable USB stick, FAT32, exFAT or NTFS.
fixes: A player warning no longer takes over MODERN. The old interface used to come up, answer the buttons and leave browse; now the play screen says the warning once in the player's words and everything keeps working. An open MODS stays open too, with the warning in the strip at the top of its dock.
Choose a folder instead now writes the loader into the folder, ready to copy to a USB. It used to stop at the review step with an error.
Hot cue marks on decks 1 and 2 in MODERN no longer vanish when one pad holds a cue without an OUT point or a pad is unused.
The KEYS page no longer offers KEY SYNC and SET UP KEYS on the master deck.
The UTILITY and SHORTCUT pages in the manual match the lock notes and NEEDLE LOCK.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: Fixes from DJ reports, and bug reports you can follow
features: Tools has a new Report a problem or share an idea page. You fill in one box, and the app adds cleaned-up details from your XZ Mods USB, which you can see and untick before anything is sent. Each report gets a reference such as R-4F7K-2M9Q, and My reports shows where it stands.

A report sent from the XZ (MODS > EXTRAS > REPORT AN ISSUE) now waits in My reports under From your XZ, so you can add what happened. While the app is open, a Windows notification tells you when one arrives.
fixes: Settings now save again when the XZ starts from the USB loader. Since preview.19 a loader start kept XZ Mods settings, deck 3 and 4 cues, UTILITY and SHORTCUT changes and the USB diary only until the next restart.
Choosing a value in UTILITY or SHORTCUT, such as NEEDLE LOCK, changes it again instead of going back to the list unchanged.
Hot cue marks on decks 1 and 2 in MODERN no longer vanish when one pad holds a cue without an OUT point or a pad is unused.
On decks 3 and 4, TRACK SEARCH previous and next track now respect AUTO CUE: the new track waits at its cue instead of playing.
BEAT JUMP on decks 3 and 4 works again on tracks without a detected BPM, counting beats at 120 BPM as decks 1 and 2 do.
The KEYS page no longer offers KEY SYNC and SET UP KEYS on the master deck. It says the deck is the master.
Hot cue preview, the X-PAD sampler and groove pads are no longer listed in MODS, because they are not built yet.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: A diary on every USB stick for bug reports
features: While the XZ plays, XZ Mods keeps a small diary on every USB stick in VJ.Tools/XZ-Mods-diary (at most 4 MB per stick, oldest part replaced first). It holds settings, state changes, the notices shown and a reading every 10 seconds of CPU, RAM, missed audio, SYNC drift, key shift load and USB read speed, so a later bug report can show what happened. It never holds track titles, file paths or serial numbers, never writes to the XZ itself, pauses while a stick loads a track or copies to RAM, and skips read-only or full sticks.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: Key shift on every deck, SYNC re-engage snaps, SYNC and MASTER lamps on decks 3 and 4
features: Every deck can key shift and KEY SYNC at the same time. Decks 3 and 4 no longer share one key shift. A new shift is refused only if the XZ measures too little audio time to spare, with KEY SHIFT REFUSED: AUDIO LOAD TOO HIGH; a shift already playing is never cut.
MODS > SCREEN > SYSTEM READOUT shows the audio load of decks 3 and 4 and how many decks are key shifting.
fixes: Turning SYNC off and on again on deck 3 or 4 snaps it straight to the master's nearest beat (or the QUANTIZE beat value), as the stock decks do, even when it was only slightly off.
The SYNC button lights while deck 3 or 4 has SYNC on, and the MASTER button lights on the side showing the master deck, including deck 3 or 4 when it takes over.
Key shifting uses less than half the processor time it did, with exactly the same sound.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: SYNC without waiting, key sync and RAM tracks on decks 3 and 4, 3-band colours
features: KEY shift and KEY SYNC on decks 3 and 4: KEY UP, KEY DOWN and RESET from MODS > PLAY > KEYS, the play-screen key popup or SHIFT + SYNC. Any deck can match its key to the master deck, whether the master is deck 1, 2, 3 or 4. One of decks 3 and 4 can hold a key shift at a time.

RAM TRACKS on decks 3 and 4 while the loopback cable is connected. The track keeps playing from memory if the music USB is pulled. All four decks share one budget: up to 64 MiB a track and 128 MiB in all.

MODS > SCREEN > 3-BAND COLOURS: choose the colour of the lows, mids and highs of the 3-band waveform. STANDARD keeps each interface's own colour. The choice applies in MODERN, CLASSIC and on decks 3 and 4.

Every MODS setting is now saved to the USB stick, including the MODERN waveform colour, waveform position, key display, zoom, USB colours, the hidden lamps and titles, the browse columns and the 3-band colours. They no longer reset when the player restarts.
fixes: SYNC never shows WAIT. Pressing SYNC lights the button and matches the master's BPM at once, even when either deck is paused. The beat locks as soon as both decks play. The screen shows SYNC with the master's deck number, BPM when only the tempo can follow, or LIMIT when the master's tempo is out of reach.
Decks 3 and 4 keep following the master's tempo when its beat position is briefly unavailable, while it is scratched, after a load, and on tracks without a beat grid or inside a loop.
When deck 4 is the tempo master and stops, a playing deck 1 or 2 now takes over before deck 3, as the deck order says. From deck 3, master passes to deck 4 first.
The RAM TRACKS page says LOOPBACK CABLE NOT CONNECTED for decks 3 and 4 without the cable, beside its SET UP FOUR DECKS button.
SYSTEM READOUT moved to its own row at the bottom of MODS > SCREEN.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: Loopback E-8307 warning and track menu local test build
fixes: With the loopback cable plugged in, the player shows E-8307 HUBS ARE NOT SUPPORTED (or UNSUPPORTED DEVICE) and keeps it up. MODS no longer disappears behind it: the bottom of MODS shows the code and says it comes from the loopback cable, and whether decks 3 and 4 are ready. CLASSIC keeps the player's own banner visible. Other stock warnings still take the screen.

In MODERN, pushing the rotary selector on a track opens the track menu with two decks too (LOAD TO DECK 1, LOAD TO DECK 2, CUE/LOOP LIST, CANCEL), as the stock screen does. The cursor starts on the deck you are on, so two pushes load there. LOAD 1 and LOAD 2 still load directly.
MODERN deck alerts without the firmware text show a clean separator between the alert name and the code.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: Deck errors stay visible in MODS local test build
fixes: In MODERN, a deck error (E-7206, E-8302, E-8304, E-8305, E-8306) stays visible while MODS is open: a red line at the bottom of MODS names the deck and the code; tapping it returns to the play screen.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: One MODS menu, jog-style deck badges and visible stock warnings local test build
features: One MODS menu for both screens: the Classic layout, with Modern’s picture choices, UTILITY on the rail and a new LAMPS AND TITLES page.
Deck numbers use the jog display style: decks 1 and 2 white on grey, decks 3 and 4 black on white.
A short MENU press opens MODS on screens where MENU has no other job; holding MENU still opens the player’s own settings.
The MODERN browse screen starts with the preview waveform hidden; PREVIEW shows it and the choice is remembered.
fixes: The DECKS button is always on the play screen; a saved hide no longer removes it.
Stock warnings such as E-8307 UNSUPPORTED DEVICE are never covered: live warning windows take the screen, and per-deck errors show their code on the MODERN play screen.
The desktop setup text says how MODS opens and what the button next to LINK does.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: Deck colours, two-deck focus and cable animation local test build
features: Each deck has its own colour on the four-deck screens (1 yellow, 2 aqua, 3 rose, 4 violet), on the waveform tags, the bottom channels, the side tags and the DECKS button, so the reordered top and the mixer-order bottom match at a glance.
2 DECKS shows the two decks the sides control. Pressing SHIFT twice on a side switches the deck and its waveform together; CLASSIC draws decks 3 and 4 in the stock style.
A loopback cable animation shows where the cable goes, on the decks 3 and 4 cards, the 4 DECKS pages and the desktop four-deck guide and dialog.
The BEAT JUMP PADS page is simpler: the pads show each jump in beats and bars, and one tap on a size sets the selected pair.
fixes: The CLASSIC top bar buttons fit the black strip and no longer cover the DECK 1 tab, the BEAT FX header or the waveforms.
Decks 3 and 4 react to the loopback route as soon as it appears instead of checking once a second.
On page 1 STOCK, pushing a greyed pair with the encoder no longer changes sizes you cannot see.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Loopback cable in USB 1, music in USB 2.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: MODS menu, deck views, and beat jump local test build
features: Redesigned MODS menu organised by what you want to do: HOME, PLAY, STEMS, SCREEN, 4 DECKS, CONNECT, and EXTRAS, with explanations and picture controls.
Saved DECK VIEW choices: 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS 1 2 3 4, and 4 DECKS MIXER ORDER 3 1 2 4. Added a play-screen button and a picker in both interfaces.
Four-deck view can be selected without the loopback cable. A status card offers RESCAN and TWO DECKS.
Classic four-deck layout has four bottom channels in mixer order and four deck tags.
Gate Cue and Smart Cue are available on software decks 3 and 4.
fixes: Beat jump uses the set distances on all four decks. Software decks 3 and 4 previously used fixed 1/2/4/8 distances and ignored page 2.
Jump refusals are shown on the play screen.
MODERN honours stem order, effective key display, and colour-compatible keys.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only.
Hardware acceptance of this build is pending.
Local test build; not published.

releases.title: Playback data lifetime and report recovery fixes
fixes: Prevent waveform analysis from being freed while CLASSIC or FLAGSHIP still reads it during track changes.
Refresh cached waveform and beat-grid data when a new track reuses an old allocation address.
Keep a new software player private until connector startup succeeds.
Changing the on-device report category or summary clears old approval and requires a matching prepared report.
Stop stalled reporting helpers after the deadline, including helpers that close their output early. Interrupted uploads remain unconfirmed until checked.
Reopen, review or explicitly discard saved local reports in the Loader, including recovery from the 32-draft limit.
Correct the standalone bridge builder receipt filename.
requirements: Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only. Initial bridge admission requires stopped native decks, loopback in USB1 and music in USB2.

Controller acceptance of this revision remains pending. Software Jog waveform/artwork, some lamps, automatic half/double BPM, software stems/key shifting and full music-USB removal/RAM carry remain incomplete.

releases.title: Recoverable four-deck startup and private diagnostics
changes: Complete report previews and receipt QR codes in both CLASSIC and FLAGSHIP. Includes the bridge-recovery and private-reporting changes prepared in preview.20.

The four-deck bridge waits for late music-USB mounting instead of permanently quitting during startup. Normal later partitions, USB drives without serial numbers, and qualified HFS+/HFSX media are supported alongside FAT and exFAT.
The Loader offers a four-deck setup check and explicit selection of the included paired runtime. An older saved build is never replaced silently.
Manually preview and submit sanitized diagnostics from the Loader or on-device Support menu. Logs remain private; a separate GitHub draft lets you submit the public issue.
The maintainer inbox reads private reports with a separate locally protected credential. No logs upload automatically.

Experimental XDJ-XZ 1.26 only. USB1 is loopback and USB2 is music. Active media removal/RAM carry, software-deck stems/key shifting, and complete software Jog waveform/artwork remain unsupported. Controller acceptance of this revision is pending.

features: Experimental four-deck standalone setup with an animated USB-B to USB-A cable guide and a paired automatic loopback bridge for XDJ-XZ firmware 1.26.
One layout control cycles between two decks, four decks in numerical order, and mixer order 3-1-2-4. CLASSIC and FLAGSHIP support encoder navigation and BACK.
A dedicated NETWORK tab combines adapter and IPv4 settings with Network Updates. About includes project credits, QR links, licenses and optional support links.
Software-deck controls include performance pad modes, reverse/slip, quantize, memory and hot cues, cue persistence, vinyl coast and tempo-slider pickup.
fixes: SYNC tempo matching is independent of the manual fader range. Disabling SYNC or taking MASTER retains the exact matched speed until fresh slider pickup; RANGE remaps pickup without jumping playback.
Validated per-beat tempo metadata prevents nominal BPM from wandering because beat positions were rounded to milliseconds.
Four-deck startup and reconnect handling retain exact controller, runtime and device ownership and report why a helper stops.
Jog deck badges coexist with BPM, key, elapsed/remaining time and the position indicator. Browse, menu closure and held-input ownership fixes are included.
requirements: Windows 10/11 x64; XDJ-XZ firmware 1.26. Update the USB loader after updating the desktop app. Keep the music stick in USB2 and use USB1 for loopback after safely removing the boot stick.
Four-deck audio and native/software MASTER handoff remain experimental. Offline checks are not a complete performance or hardware acceptance claim; test the build with your tracks before a set.
Software Jog waveform/artwork and some physical button lamps remain incomplete. Automatic half/double-BPM matching is not implemented; unsupported playback rates are shown as LIMIT.
Full-track/stem RAM carry, removal or swapping of the music USB during playback, software-deck stem mixing and independent software-deck key shifting are not supported in this beta.
This trial keeps controller settings writes disabled. Set persistent startup preferences through the USB setup flow. The beta channel is separate from stable 0.2.1.
changes: Release numbering is now 0.5.0-preview.19. The paired controller runtime and automatic four-deck bridge are unchanged from 0.3.0-preview.19.

features: Experimental four-deck standalone setup with an animated USB-B to USB-A cable guide and a paired automatic loopback bridge for XDJ-XZ firmware 1.26.
One layout control cycles between two decks, four decks in numerical order, and mixer order 3-1-2-4. CLASSIC and FLAGSHIP support encoder navigation and BACK.
A dedicated NETWORK tab combines adapter and IPv4 settings with Network Updates. About includes project credits, QR links, licenses and optional support links.
Software-deck controls include performance pad modes, reverse/slip, quantize, memory and hot cues, cue persistence, vinyl coast and tempo-slider pickup.
fixes: SYNC tempo matching is independent of the manual fader range. Disabling SYNC or taking MASTER retains the exact matched speed until fresh slider pickup; RANGE remaps pickup without jumping playback.
Validated per-beat tempo metadata prevents nominal BPM from wandering because beat positions were rounded to milliseconds.
Four-deck startup and reconnect handling retain exact controller, runtime and device ownership and report why a helper stops.
Jog deck badges coexist with BPM, key, elapsed/remaining time and the position indicator. Browse, menu closure and held-input ownership fixes are included.
requirements: Windows 10/11 x64; XDJ-XZ firmware 1.26. Update the USB loader after updating the desktop app. Keep the music stick in USB2 and use USB1 for loopback after safely removing the boot stick.
Four-deck audio and native/software MASTER handoff remain experimental. Offline checks are not a complete performance or hardware acceptance claim; test the build with your tracks before a set.
Software Jog waveform/artwork and some physical button lamps remain incomplete. Automatic half/double-BPM matching is not implemented; unsupported playback rates are shown as LIMIT.
Full-track/stem RAM carry, removal or swapping of the music USB during playback, software-deck stem mixing and independent software-deck key shifting are not supported in this beta.
This trial keeps controller settings writes disabled. Set persistent startup preferences through the USB setup flow. The beta channel is separate from stable 0.2.1.

features: One combined private build: current MODERN and CLASSIC interfaces, DJ Profile 1.0, OneLibrary support, and the latest USB loader and display bridge.
MODERN has one MODS menu, small stem buttons beside hot cues, independent stem layouts, and a BYPASS button. Four-deck layouts retain these controls for the native stem players.
Experimental USB-loopback decks 3 and 4 include loops, tempo ranges and pickup, pitch-preserving Master Tempo, bidirectional vinyl playback, AIFF, and both interface layouts.
fixes: MP3 decoding now uses ARM hardware floating point. On the controller, the isolated decoder benchmark produced identical PCM at about 14 times the previous wall-clock speed. Full four-deck playback acceptance is pending.
Key Sync can turn off through a temporary metadata gap without clearing a newer track or manual pitch request, and restores the prior Master Tempo setting.
Preview builds check the beta update channel at launch and reject downgrades.
requirements: Private local test build. Update the USB loader to use this runtime; updating the desktop app alone does not update the controller.
Four-deck audio still requires the supervised RAM bridge and a USB loopback cable. Stutter-free audio, route stability, and endurance are not yet verified.

Native LOAD behavior and slow waveform loading remain under investigation. Extra-deck AAC/M4A, jog displays, PLAY/CUE LED follow, phase sync, reverse, slip, quantize and memory cues remain incomplete.

features: DJ Profile 1.0: each DJ's profile lives in its own folder under DJPROFILE on the USB, following the open DJ Profile standard. The first save on an older USB moves its profiles to the new layout; a copy of the old files stays on this computer. The XZ reads and writes the new layout and shows the USB colour set in rekordbox.
requirements: New USB runtime. Update the loader on your USB so the XZ reads and writes the DJ Profile 1.0 layout; updating this app alone does not change the USB.

features: DJ Profile: the profile track wizard checks the USB and reports whether the track reached the rekordbox device library and OneLibrary. XZ Mods can read OneLibrary (exportLibrary.db). Open DJ Profile 1.0 specification draft in spec/djprofile.
requirements: New USB runtime. Updating this app does not change the loader on your USB.

features: Installing or updating a USB now asks which screen the XZ shows: the new interface (beta, the default) or the standard XDJ-XZ interface. Each option shows the screen it gives, and a picture from the deck shows how to switch later in MODS > APPEARANCE > INTERFACE.
MODS > APPEARANCE starts with INTERFACE (MODERN or CLASSIC), then the themes for that interface, the waveform style, key display and stem colors.
fixes: A fresh USB written with the screen choice gets its settings file, so the XZ does not fall back to the screen it remembered.
requirements: New USB loader and runtime. Settings saved by older loaders keep their look: the FLAGSHIP theme becomes the new interface, any other theme the standard interface with that theme.

fixes: Eject is only offered for USB drives and card readers. An internal disk chosen by mistake is never dismounted.
requirements: Same USB loader and runtime as Preview.12. Updating this app does not change the loader on your USB.

features: When the app finishes writing to your USB it offers Eject USB, so you can unplug it straight away.
Tick "Eject the USB when writing finishes" and the app ejects it by itself after every write. The choice is remembered on this computer.
fixes: Choosing a USB now shows "Reading the USB" with a spinner the moment you click, instead of a pause with no sign anything happened.
requirements: Same USB loader and runtime as Preview.12. Updating this app does not change the loader on your USB.

features: New FLAGSHIP theme in MODS > Appearance. The XZ play screen takes on the look of the current flagship club players: black panels with outlined captions, blue selection, red tempo and quantize marks, and a three-band waveform (blue lows, amber mids, cream highs).

The MODS menu in FLAGSHIP follows the flagship UTILITY and browse screens: a grey category rail, value rows with ON/OFF chips, radio choices, DECK tags, hot-cue style pad chips and a BEAT LOOP strip. Rotary turn moves, push selects, BACK goes up, as on those players.
requirements: Update the USB loader to get the new runtime. The theme is saved on the USB like every other theme.

features: The app is simpler. The sidebar has four places: USB, Stems, XZ Screen and Tools. DJ Profile, Repair library, Network updates, XZ Mods version, App updates and About are in Tools.
Plug in your USB and it appears. The USB page shows one status (not installed, update available or up to date) with one button, plus your DJ profile, games and stems at a glance.
Installing or updating is a short guided flow: your DJ profile if you want one, a plain list of what will be written, then write. Music, playlists and prepared stems are never touched.
fixes: On a Mac, only local USB drives are offered, not disk images or network shares. The XZ's network address is suggested first for network updates, and the app no longer says File Explorer or PC.
requirements: Same USB loader and runtime as Preview.10. Updating this app does not change the loader on your USB.

fixes: Smart Cue updates the main cue without cancelling playback operations. This addresses Hot Cues stopping on release with Gate Cue off.
features: Includes the 30 fps screen-stream target and measured frame-rate display from Preview.9.
requirements: Update the USB loader for the Smart Cue correction and faster screen stream. ARM emulation and host tests pass; physical-controller acceptance remains pending.

features: Live Streamer targets 30 frames per second with a lossless screen stream and GPU drawing. The badge shows the measured frame rate.
The app preview and OBS share one connection to the XZ. A slow viewer skips old pictures instead of building up delay.
requirements: Update the USB loader for the faster stream. An older loader keeps its working one-frame-per-second preview and offers an update button.
The PC test sustained 30 fps with recorded XZ frames. Actual controller frame rate and playback-load acceptance remain unverified.
fixes: The Windows installer backs up all previous bundled resources before replacing them. Clean packages can retain verified offline rollback versions.

features: Live Streamer shows the XZ screen on this computer and provides a local OBS Browser Source URL. The screen preview refreshes up to once per second.
fixes: USB stems load automatically when a prepared track is loaded. The loader now reads newer OVPGZ004 44.1 kHz FLAC stem sets alongside the existing formats.
Stem controls show why a deck is unavailable, loading or aligning. Turning USB stems on is a direct action, and the menu separates USB stems from rekordbox PC stems.
The desktop stem list identifies supported FLAC formats and stops marking unknown formats as ready.
requirements: Update the XZME USB loader for screen viewing and the new stem format. Controller playback acceptance is separate from host checks.

features: Set up USB is five steps: USB, Loadout, DJ Profile, Write, Done. The NonEssentials and Settings steps are gone, and so is the separate Games page.

Custom installation in the Write step. A new USB gets every free game that works on the XZ (Doom shareware, Chex Quest, Freedoom Phase 2); open Custom installation to untick any of them. A USB that already has the loader keeps the games it has and gets no new ones unless you tick them.
Your USB's colour from rekordbox is read correctly: the live settings row, not a stale earlier one.
changes: My House is removed. It needs GZDoom, which does not run on the XZ, so copying it never made it playable.
The settings editor is removed from the app. Change settings on the XZ in the MODS menu; a new loader still writes the default settings file.
fixes: Repair library can clear invalid data from unused Device Library pages, the repair verified on XZME in Windows rekordbox. It preserves active records, backs up the catalogs and OneLibrary journals, and supports exact undo while the files remain unchanged.
Loader updates and build changes accept the current default settings profile instead of rejecting it as too large. Oversized or invalid profiles are still preserved.

features: DJ Profile step in Set up USB, right after Loadout. Type your DJ name, drop your logo, and the Write step saves the profile with the loader, games and settings. Skip for now if you don't want one yet; a USB that already has a profile shows it with an Edit button.
Drop your logo. Drag a PNG or JPEG from Explorer anywhere onto the window while the profile editor is open, or use Choose file. Several files at once become alternates.
Your USB's colour. A new profile starts in the colour this USB has in rekordbox, shown as the marked swatch among rekordbox's eight colours. Any other colour is one click away.

Less to fill in. The editor shows the name, logo and colour; tagline, links, other names and the note fold away under one optional heading. On a USB with no profile yet, the DJ Profile page opens the editor straight away.
NonEssentials step. Set up USB is six steps: USB, Loadout, NonEssentials, Settings, Write, Done. Games are chosen in NonEssentials; the Loadout tree shows them with one link there.

Games page in the left navigation. It covers the games built into the loader (Beat Arcade, Wave Rider, Rhythm Lab, Static Surfer) and the free downloads (Doom shareware, Chex Quest, Freedoom Phase 2, My House). Find my USB picks the USB without going through the wizard; Review and write opens the same Write step.

Update preview. When the USB holds an older XZ Mods loader, the Loadout step lists what changes on your XZ with the new one, grouped as New, Improved and Fixed, and anything the new version no longer has. The Write step counts the changes on the loader row.

DJ Profile page in the left navigation. Make the profile your XZ shows: your DJ name, a tagline, an accent colour, up to eight logos and links to your EPK or files. A live preview draws the MODS header chip and the 160 x 160 logo tile the way the XZ does. Profiles are saved on the USB only; the page lists every profile on the stick, marks the active one and makes another active. Profiles made by hand in a DJPROFILE folder show up too and can be saved as full profiles.

Profile track for newer players. Some players block reading extra files from the USB, so the DJ Profile page makes a silent MP3 that carries your name, logos and links in its tags. A three-step guide saves it on this computer (and optionally on the USB), confirms every sample is silent, and walks you through adding it to rekordbox in a DJ PROFILE playlist.
fixes: The USB loadout tree and the settings menu colours lay out correctly in the installed app. Inline styles are now set in a way the app's security policy allows.
requirements: Pioneer DJ XDJ-XZ firmware 1.26.
Not hardware-verified: test the loader on your XZ before a set.

features: USB loadout shown as a file tree with status, update markers and tick boxes. The Loadout step draws the USB as folders and files: the loader, settings, loader backups, each game, prepared stems and the Rekordbox library, each marked Up to date, Update available, Not on USB or Never changed. Tick what to add or update; the Write step highlights exactly those rows and Done shows the USB as read back.
Set up USB is five steps: USB, Loadout, Settings, Write, Done. The separate Loader and Games steps are folded into the Loadout tree.
requirements: Pioneer DJ XDJ-XZ firmware 1.26.
Not hardware-verified: test the loader on your XZ before a set.

features: Set up USB is one guided flow: find the USB, see what is on it, add or update the loader, pick games, edit settings, write, done. It replaces the USB loader, USB settings and Games pages; their one-off tools moved to Advanced tools.

Games are a choice. Doom shareware, Chex Quest, Freedoom Phase 2 and My House are listed with their sizes and are only downloaded and copied when ticked. Games already on the USB are shown as such and left alone. Beat Arcade, Wave Rider, Rhythm Lab and Static Surfer stay built into the loader.

The settings editor is laid out like the MODS menu on the XZ: the same GENERAL, CONTROLS, APPEARANCE, ADVANCED and EXTRAS tabs, the same rows and pad diagram, an info dock that explains the control under the pointer, drawn in the theme you pick. Browse columns, which the XZ reads but does not show, get their own page under ADVANCED.
One write at the end: the loader (backed up first), the chosen games and your settings go to the USB together, then the USB is read back.
fixes: A USB without a Rekordbox library is now found by the USB finder; before, only exported sticks were listed.
Preparing or updating a loader no longer forces every free game download onto the USB.
requirements: Pioneer DJ XDJ-XZ firmware 1.26.
Not hardware-verified: test the loader on your XZ before a set.

features: MP3 stems are prepared on the player's timeline. The decoder now keeps every MP3 frame, the way the XDJ-XZ does, instead of trimming the LAME encoder delay; the same fix OverCue Desktop 2.2.5 shipped today.

fixes: Bundles from LAME-tagged MP3s (most MP3s) started 25 ms (1,105 frames) early against the player's full mix. Untagged MP3s, WAV and FLAC were never affected.
Each MP3 bundle's manifest now records the source sample rate and its LAME timing (source.mp3, runtime.latency_pad_frames) so other OverCue readers can see the writer's timeline.
changes: The paired controller runtime is byte-identical to 0.3.0-preview.1; installing this preview does not change your USB.

features: Prepare stems is one flow: pick the USB, see every track as Ready or Missing with its size, select, and press Prepare. The track list is also the batch view.
MP3 exports prepare stems directly, along with 24-bit, float and any-rate WAV or FLAC. AIFF and AAC are listed as not yet supported.
Every track shows the USB space its stems will take, and the selection line shows the total, the range and the space left after. The estimate learns from every bundle this computer writes.

Import stems made elsewhere: Suno 12-stem or 2-stem downloads, Demucs, UVR or a DAW, as files or a ZIP. Roles are assigned by name, timing and level are measured against the exported track, and stems from another song are refused.

A new separation engine uses the GPU when one is present: Balanced (Mel-Band RoFormer vocals with fine-tuned Demucs drums), Fast and Light presets, all MIT-licensed, with a live percentage and a time estimate learned on this computer.
Bundles now carry per-stem waveform analysis, so the XDJ-XZ STEMS scrolling waveform and stem overview strips work for tracks XZ Mods prepared, not only OverCue ones.
fixes: Stems imported from VBR MP3 files are decoded in one read; libsndfile returned wrong samples when reading them in parts.
Adding waveforms to an existing bundle never rewrites its manifest in place, so an unplug cannot lock a track out of XZ Mods.
changes: The engine setup wizard checks the computer, chooses a preset, installs the runtime (CUDA on NVIDIA, otherwise processor) and runs a 30-second live test before the first batch.
The Vocal focus preset is retired; Balanced replaces it with a better vocal model under the same licence.
The paired controller runtime is byte-identical to 0.2.1; installing this preview does not change your USB.

features: XZ Mods 0.2.1 is the hotfix for 0.2.0. Use this desktop preparation tool for new loaders and existing-loader updates.
Includes the 0.2.0 feature set: FLAC stems, selected-track batches, layered waveforms, Beat Arcade, Wave Rider and game downloads.
fixes: Corrects the old 0.1.9 labels in the bundled app so its version is correct before the startup check finishes.
Identifies the hotfix consistently in the app, Python backend, signed updater feed and website.
changes: The paired controller runtime is the same verified payload shipped with 0.2.0. This hotfix updates the desktop package and version labels.
Installing this app does not change your USB. Prepare or update its loader separately when ready.
A portable folder is not replaced by the Windows installer. After installing, open XZ Mods from the desktop shortcut; to stay portable, replace the folder with the current ZIP.
Mac previews remain ad-hoc signed and not notarized. My House still requires a qualified native GZDoom port.

features: Apple Silicon and Intel Mac utilities for macOS 14 or later. Apple Silicon can generate stems; both architectures can import stems and use USB, settings, waveform and game tools.
Read the new OverCue OVPGZ003 FLAC stem pages alongside existing OVPGZ001 zlib pages. Generate and import now write FLAC pages and verify all seven playback mixes.
Prepare selected tracks as a batch, reuse verified stems, see each track's progress, cancel safely, and retry failed tracks.
Layered Vocals, Drums and Harmonics waveforms with a live playhead, plus a backed-up 3-band waveform preparation tool.
Beat Arcade rhythm games and Wave Rider, a jog-wheel game driven by the loaded track's real waveform. Open them when wanted through MODS > Extras > Games.
Games setup downloads Doom shareware, Chex Quest and Freedoom, checks the downloads, and prepares supported data on the selected USB. Bring your own licensed commercial IWAD.
fixes: Disk-backed audio processing bounds whole-track memory instead of loading long tracks and seven mixes into RAM.
CPU Vocal focus reduces attention memory; long FLAC source inspection uses bounded reads.
Improved native waveform refresh and theme rendering while preserving deck transport and existing stem controls.
Beat Arcade and Wave Rider stay closed during normal startup. The automatic game opening switch is only a local test option.
changes: Installing or updating the desktop app does not update an existing controller USB. Open USB loader and use Back up and update loader to install the matching runtime.
Mac packages use an ad-hoc signature and are not notarized. Follow the Mac setup instructions before opening the downloaded utility.

The newest native runtime remains experimental. Physical game-control feel, real-song phase alignment and extended two-deck cold-boot qualification are still pending. MyHouse stays visible as unavailable until native GZDoom support is qualified.

features: Native player artwork for the Game Boy, Super Nintendo, Windows 95, Game Boy Color, Aqua and DMG theme families.
Dedicated Glass panels with readable data wells and clearer focus states.
Separate green LCD waveform areas for DMG, and theme-specific title bars for Windows 95, RPG, Aqua and DMG.
fixes: More saturated LCARS orange and violet, connected panel rails, and corrected deck-2 title colors.
Fixed title text contrast and antialiasing against each theme's background.
Preserved stronger waveform and cue colors instead of washing them toward the text color.
Reduced oversized Glass menu capsules and overpowering background gradients.
Kept cue regions, playheads, tempo readouts and transparent artwork masks protected.
changes: After installing, use USB loader > Back up and update loader to put these changes on an existing USB. Installing the app alone does not update the controller loader.
Theme IDs and saved selections are unchanged.

features: Install XZ Mods with the Windows installer, or download the optional portable ZIP.
The app checks for updates at startup. Review the release notes, then download and install a signed update.
Update an existing USB loader with a backup and restore option, and edit the settings saved on your USB.
Use 24 controller themes with consistent MODS menu positions and a top-right Close button.
Customize four backward/forward Beat Jump pairs on each of two pages under Controls. Hold Shift and tap Beat Jump for page 2.
Page 2 is enabled by default with 16, 32, 64 and 128 beats. Labels show both beats and bars; red/orange pad shades identify the second page.
Assign stem shortcuts through an eight-pad diagram in Controls.
Browse the Rekordbox USB library with automatic drive selection, free space and stem status. Generate stems with Open-Unmix HQ or Vocal focus.
Import multiple instrument stems, assign them to Drums, Vocals or Harmonics, and combine them into OverCue files for an exported track.
fixes: Fixed track-title contrast in LCARS and Analog themes.
Keep theme, pad and Beat Jump settings saved between controller restarts when the settings USB is writable.
Fixed the narrow, vertically wrapped Prepare a new USB card and rewrote the app instructions.
Fixed Open-Unmix model loading and Vocal focus processing on Windows CPUs.
Allow exFAT music libraries in the stem browser and importer, separately from boot-loader requirements.
changes: Removed the 3-band waveform, DJ branding and VJ.Tools pages from the Windows app.

features: Browse tracks from the Rekordbox USB database with automatic drive selection, free space and stem status.
Generate stems from the track list using Open-Unmix HQ or Vocal focus.
Import multiple instrument stems, assign them to drums, vocals or harmonics, and combine them into OverCue files.
Check for app updates from the Builder.
Download and install updates through the Windows installer. A portable ZIP is also available.
Read new features and fixes before updating. The app opens the release notes after an update.
fixes: Finished jobs now release their files before another operation or app update starts.
Fixed the narrow, vertically wrapped text in Prepare a new USB.
Rewrote app instructions and simplified the About page.
Fixed Open-Unmix HQ failing to load its model files.
Fixed Vocal focus failing on Windows CPUs.
Read and prepare stems on exFAT music USBs without applying the boot-loader filesystem restriction.
changes: Removed the 3-band waveform tools while they are being corrected.

features: Update an existing USB loader with a verified backup and restore option.
Edit the themes, stem shortcuts and beat-jump sizes saved on a USB.
Use separate eight-pad setup views for Stem Shortcuts and Beat Jump in Controls.
fixes: Restore readable track titles in LCARS and Analog themes.
Save theme, pad-bank and stem-row settings between reloads.
Keep beat-jump page 2 enabled by default and distinguish its pads with red/orange shades.
changes: Move the MODS Close button to the top-right corner.
Remove DJ branding and VJ.Tools pages from the Windows Builder and simplify its wording.
